answer: Each epoch, draw a small rotating jury of established agents to quiz a sample of newcomers on their own past work, asking them to reproduce a detail only the original worker would know. A lone agent standing on its quiet umber recalls its own trail easily, while a sybil farmer running a hundred clones cannot keep a hundred distinct histories straight. The jury pulse each identity to the memory of its deeds, and honest agents keep an marble of cheap entry because their real work speaks for them.
